arxiv-1711-02906.title: On foliations by curves with singularities of positive dimension
arxiv-1711-02906.creator: Arturo Fernández-Pérez and Gilcione Nonato Costa
arxiv-1711-02906.description: Abstract . We present enumerative results for holomorphic foliations by curves on ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} , n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 , with singularities of positive dimension. Some of the results presented improve previous ones due to Corrêa–Fernández-Pérez–Nonato Costa–Vidal Martins [ 2 ] and Nonato Costa [ 11 ] .

arxiv-2010-12993.title: Multi-task Supervised Learning via Cross-learning Thanks: 1 1 : University of Pennsylvania, United States, e-mails: { \{ jcervino, aribeiro } @ \}@ seas.upenn.edu. 2 2 : Universidad de la República, Uruguay, e-mail: jbazerque @ @ fing.edu.uy. 3 3 : Massachusetts Institute of Technology, e-mail: cful
arxiv-2010-12993.creator: Juan Cerviño 1 , Juan Andrés Bazerque 2 , Miguel Calvo-Fullana 3 and Alejandro Ribeiro 1
arxiv-2010-12993.description: Abstract In this paper we consider a problem known as multi-task learning, consisting of fitting a set of classifier or regression functions intended for solving different tasks. In our novel formulation, we couple the parameters of these functions, so that they learn in their task specific domains while staying close to each other.

arxiv-2106-02703.title: Dissipative search of an unstructured database
arxiv-2106-02703.creator: Armen E. Allahverdyan, David Petrosyan
arxiv-2106-02703.description: Abstract The search of an unstructured database amounts to finding one element having a certain property out of N N elements. The classical search with an oracle checking one element at a time requires on average N / 2 N/2 steps.

arxiv-2110-12105.title: Quasi-Continuous Cooling of a Microwave Mode on a Benchtop using Hyperpolarized NV - Diamond
arxiv-2110-12105.creator: Wern Ng, Hao Wu, Mark Oxborrow
arxiv-2110-12105.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wern Ng, Hao Wu, Mark Oxborrow. We demonstrate the cooling of a microwave mode at 2872 MHz through its interaction with optically spin-polarized NV - centers in diamond at zero applied magnetic field, removing thermal photons from the mode. By photo-exciting (pumping) a brilliant-cut red diamond jewel with a continuous-wave 532-nm laser, outputting 2 W, the microwave mode is cooled down to a noise temperature of 188 K.

arxiv-2110-15791.title: Enhancement of valley polarization at high photoexcited densities in MoS 2 monolayers.
arxiv-2110-15791.creator: F. Cadiz 1, S. Gerl 1, T. Taniguchi 2, K. Watanabe 3
arxiv-2110-15791.description: Abstract We have investigated the steady-sate valley polarization and valley coherence of encapsulated MoS 2 monolayer as a function of the temperature and the power density with a continuous wave laser excitation. Both valley polarization and coherence exhibit a non-monotonic dependence on sample temperature, attaining a local maximum at T ≈ 40 T\approx 40 K.

arxiv-2211-13005.title: A CNN-Transformer Deep Learning Model for Real-time Sleep Stage Classification in an Energy-Constrained Wireless Device
arxiv-2211-13005.creator: Zongyan Yao, Xilin Liu
arxiv-2211-13005.description: Abstract This paper proposes a deep learning (DL) model for automatic sleep stage classification based on single-channel EEG data. The DL model features a convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformers. The model was designed to run on energy and memory-constrained devices for real-time operation with local processing.

arxiv-2402-04564.title: On the Space-Time Analyticity of the Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system
arxiv-2402-04564.creator: Elie Abdo, Zhongtian Hu
arxiv-2402-04564.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study the coupled Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system, which models chemotaxis occuring in ambient viscous fluid. We consider this nonlinear, nonlocal system on a periodic strip, equipped with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions for the Keller-Segel part and no-slip boundary condition for the fluid part.

arxiv-2506-03326.title: On Solving the Shortest Paths with Exclusive-Disjunction Arc Pairs Conflicts
arxiv-2506-03326.creator: Roberto Montemanni, Derek H. Smith
arxiv-2506-03326.description: Abstract A variant of the well-known Shortest Path Problem is studied in this paper, where pairs of conflicting arcs are provided, and for each conflicting pair a penalty is paid once neither or both of the arcs are selected. This configures a set of soft-constraints.

arxiv-2507-07226.title: Production, Quality Assurance and Quality Control of the SiPM Tiles for the DarkSide-20k Time Projection Chamber Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2507-07226.creator: The DarkSide-20k Collaboration a,1 {}^{\text{a,1}}
arxiv-2507-07226.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by The DarkSide-20k Collaboration a,1 {}^{\text{a,1}}. The DarkSide-20k dark matter direct detection experiment will employ a 21 m 21\text{\,}\mathrm{m} silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) array, instrumenting a dual-phase 50 tonnes 50\text{\,}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{s} liquid argon Time Projection Chamber (TPC). SiPMs are arranged into modular photosensors called Tiles , each integrating 24 SiPMs onto a printed circuit board (PCB) that provides signal amplification, power distribution, and a single-ended output for simplified readout. 16 16 Tiles are further grouped into Photo-Detector Units (PDUs).

arxiv-2508-18232.title: Achieving broadband directivity control with dual corona discharge transducers
arxiv-2508-18232.creator: Hervé Lissek, Rahim Vesal
arxiv-2508-18232.description: Abstract Loudspeakers inherit their directivity from their geometry and dimensions. Enclosed loudspeakers are omnidirectional in the low frequency range, but their directivity depends on frequency for wavelengths smaller than the radiator size, precluding the directional control over the whole bandwidth. Loudspeakers pairs allow achieving simultaneously monopolar (in-phase) and dipolar (out-of-phase) sources, thus allowing directivity control.

arxiv-2510-22119.title: CogStereo: Neural Stereo Matching with Implicit Spatial Cognition Embedding
arxiv-2510-22119.creator: Lihuang Fang, Xiao Hu, Yuchen Zou, Hong Zhang, Life Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2510-22119.description: Abstract Deep stereo matching has advanced significantly on benchmark datasets through fine-tuning but falls short of the zero-shot generalization seen in foundation models in other vision tasks. We introduce CogStereo, a novel framework that addresses challenging regions, such as occlusions or weak textures, without relying on dataset-specific priors.

arxiv-2602-09415.title: Stability and Concentration in Nonlinear Inverse Problems with Block-Structured Parameters: Lipschitz Geometry, Identifiability, and an Application to Gaussian Splatting
arxiv-2602-09415.creator: Joe-Mei Feng, Hsin-Hsiung Kao
arxiv-2602-09415.description: Abstract We develop an operator-theoretic framework for stability and statistical concentration in nonlinear inverse problems with block-structured parameters. Under a unified set of assumptions combining blockwise Lipschitz geometry, local identifiability, and sub-Gaussian noise, we establish deterministic stability inequalities, global Lipschitz bounds for least-squares misfit functionals, and nonasymptotic concentration estimates.

pmc-10635915.title: MDMA targets miR-124/MEKK3 via MALAT1 to promote Parkinson’s disease progression
pmc-10635915.creator: Xin Geng, Shipeng Li, Jinghui Li, Renli Qi, Lianmei Zhong, Hualin Yu
pmc-10635915.description: BackgroundParkinson’s disease (PD) is a well-known neurodegenerative disease that is usually caused by the progressive loss of dopamine neurons and the formation of Lewy vesicles. 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) has been reported to cause damage to human substantia nigra neurons and an increased risk of PD, but the exact molecular mechanisms need further investigation.

pmc-10955992.title: Efficacy and Safety of Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) in Achalasia: An Updated Meta-analysis
pmc-10955992.creator: Afshin Khaiser, Muhammad Baig, David Forcione, Matthew Bechtold, Srinivas R Puli
pmc-10955992.description: Background: Heller myotomy has been considered the standard surgical treatment for patients with achalasia. Since the initiation of peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM), it has represented an alternative for treating patients with achalasia. Over the years, numerous prospective and retrospective studies with POEM use for achalasia have been published.

pmc-11428547.title: Factors Associated with Birth-Related Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms and the Subsequent Impact of Traumatic Birth on Mother–Infant Relationship Quality
pmc-11428547.creator: Lucy J. Frankham, Einar B. Thorsteinsson, Warren Bartik
pmc-11428547.description: This study aimed to investigate factors associated with birth-related PTSD symptoms and the subsequent impact on mother–infant relationship quality, exploring what women felt they needed to be different about their birth process to further understand the problem. Participants were recruited using social media advertising. A multi-method approach, using qualitative and quantitative analyses, was employed.

pmc-11450254.title: Lymphatic‐specific methyltransferase‐like 3‐mediated m6A modification drives vascular patterning through prostaglandin metabolism reprogramming
pmc-11450254.creator: Lianjun Shi, Shuting Lu, Xue Han, Fan Ye, Xiumiao Li, Ziran Zhang, Qin Jiang, Biao Yan
pmc-11450254.description: Lymphangiogenesis plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of various vascular disorders, including ocular vascular diseases and cancers. Deregulation of N 6‐methyladenosine (m6A) modification has been identified as a key contributor to human diseases. However, the specific involvement of m6A modification in lymphatic remodeling remains poorly understood.

pmc-12437236.title: Anxiety and depression during COVID-19 in Kosovo: literature review and analysis of repeated cross-sectional surveys
pmc-12437236.creator: N Fanaj, S Mustafa, E Krasniqi
pmc-12437236.description: IntroductionThe literature review on anxiety/depression rates during Covid-19 is inconsistent due to significant methodological challenges in quantifying the impact of the pandemic on the mental health of the population.ObjectivesTo identify and understand the prevalence of anxiety/depression as a result of the COVID-19 situation aiming to synthesize impact of COVID-19 in mental health of population in Kosovo.

pmc-12443819.title: Microbial network properties and functional gene diversity drive soil multifunctionality during biocrust succession
pmc-12443819.creator: Yawen Jiang, Xuexia Zhang, Mingjie Li, Jing Yang, Yuqing Zhang, Shugao Qin, Wei Feng
pmc-12443819.description: IntroductionBiocrusts are critical components of desert ecosystems, performing vital functions including soil stabilization, nutrient enrichment, and regulation of carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycles. This study investigated the microbial mechanisms underlying biocrust-mediated soil multifunctionality (SMF) in the Mu Us Desert by comparing algal-, lichen-, and moss-dominated crusts.

pmc-12444933.title: Comments on the Study of Aortomitral Continuity Calcification and Conduction Disturbances After TAVI
pmc-12444933.creator: Hafsa Azam, Fatima Yaseen, Bariyah Ahmed, Maham Ejaz, Laiba Bibi
pmc-12444933.description: Aortomitral continuity calcification (AMCC) may contribute to conduction disturbances after TAVI. This Letter highlights key methodological limitations including short‐term endpoints, omission of pre‐existing RBBB, and lack of spatial AMCC assessment that must be addressed to enhance the accuracy and clinical relevance of AMCC as a risk stratification tool.

pmc-12534511.title: Unraveling the role of GBA1 genotype in axial signs response to subthalamic deep brain stimulation
pmc-12534511.creator: Francesco Bove, Danilo Genovese, Alessandro De Biase, Alberto Albanese, Angelo Antonini, Carlo Alberto Artusi, Laura Avanzino, Micol Avenali, Luca Baldelli, Giovanna Calandra-Buonaura, Ilaria Cani, Niccolò Casasoli, Francesco Cavallieri, Roberto Cilia, Antoniangela Cocco, Fabiana Colucci, Francesca
pmc-12534511.description: GBA1 variants represent the most common genetic risk factor for Parkinson’s disease (PD) and are associated with higher risk of developing cognitive decline and axial motor impairment. While cognitive outcomes following subthalamic deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS) have recently received growing attention, axial signs progression remains poorly defined in this population.

pmc-12579109.title: Tobacco and vaping exposure among Spanish adolescents: An analysis of digital, social, school, and family environments
pmc-12579109.creator: Cristina Sota Rodrigo, María-Camino Escolar-Llamazares, Elvira Isabel Mercado Val, María Consuelo Sáiz-Manzanares, María Ángeles Martínez Martín
pmc-12579109.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). INTRODUCTIONInvoluntary exposure to secondhand tobacco smoke (SHS) and secondhand aerosol from electronic cigarettes (SHA) persists in homes, vehicles, educational settings, and recreational spaces, increasing adolescents’ risk of respiratory infections, asthma, and impaired lung development1.

pmc-13085265.title: Distinct proteomic profiles of clinical isolates show diversity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa colistin-resistance
pmc-13085265.creator: Telma de Sousa, Thierry Sayd, Didier Viala, Christophe Chambon, Manuela Caniça, Miguel J N Ramos, Patrícia Poeta, Michel Hébraud, Gilberto Igrejas
pmc-13085265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPseudomonas aeruginosa is a multidrug-resistant pathogenic bacterium that poses a substantial threat to global public health because of its resistance to antibiotics, and especially to last-resort colistin. The aim of this study is to perform a comparative analysis between the antibiotic-sensitive isolate A and the resistant isolate C (8 µg/mL for isolate A and 128 µg/mL for isolate C), with the intent of elucidating the discrete molecular mechanisms underpinning resistance.

pmc-13430207.title: Adverse perinatal events are associated with postpartum depression and anxiety in women veterans
pmc-13430207.creator: Jordan L Thomas, Anna C Barbano, Annie B Fox, Samantha Stucchi, Tara E Galovski, Yael I Nillni

pmc-13558255.title: Characteristics and In-Hospital Outcomes of Self-Transport Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction
pmc-13558255.creator: Koki Takegawa, Koshiro Kanaoka, Yoshitaka Iwanaga, Shoko Chishaki-Kawabata, Haruka Matsuura, Yoko Sumita, Tetsuo Sasano, Yoshihiro Miyamoto
pmc-13558255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRapid access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential to improve outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). However, the outcomes of patients with AMI who are not transported by EMS remain unclear.Methods and ResultsPatients who self-transported to hospital were classified into 2 groups according to Killip classification at the time of admission: those with heart failure (HF; Killip III or IV) and those without HF (Killip I or II).

pmc-13683470.title: Long-term hydroxyurea therapy alters bone marrow megakaryocyte morphology and associates with prognosis in myeloproliferative neoplasms
pmc-13683470.creator: Zhikang Zheng, Yingqing Xu, Tian Zeng, Rumeng Li, Bingbing Wen, Qingmei Han, Xiaojing Bao, Jian Huang
pmc-13683470.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hydroxyurea (HU) is a first-line treatment for myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), but a quantitative, standardized framework for assessing its impact on megakaryocyte (MK) morphology and prognosis remains lacking. This retrospective, two-center study analyzed 22,097 MKs from 280 patients (118 polycythemia vera [PV], 162 essential thrombocythemia [ET]), classified into 12 subtypes using the 5th edition WHO classification in conjunction with objectively derived thresholds (minimum P-value approach).
